title: Composable stream decorators and safe handler fallback contracts for Python SDK
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: build a composable decorator stack and a first-class fallback contract for Python streaming chat handlers so SDK consumers can safely layer transforms (decoding, enrichment, telemetry) and provide robust fallback behaviors when a handler fails or transport is interrupted.

Goals:
- Provide a minimal, explicit API that composes reusable decorators around a user handler without surprising ordering semantics.
- Define a well-documented fallback contract (fallback chain + circuit-aware hints) that handlers and apps can implement for graceful degradation (e.g., switch to non-streaming completion, return partial summary, or invoke cached prefix).
- Ensure backpressure and cancel semantics are preserved across decorator boundaries and that diagnostic context (diagnostic token stamps) flows with events for observability.

Constraints / Non-goals:
- This work does not change transport protocols (SSE/Websocket) or server behavior; it is SDK surface and helper primitives only.
- Not addressing C#/Go SDKs in this ticket; design notes will be shareable for cross-lang parity later.

API sketch (prototype):
- types: Event = Dict[str, Any]  # stream event envelope (kept generic for now)
- decorator: Callable[[Callable[[Event], None]], Callable[[Event], None]]
- compose_decorators(decorators: List[Callable]) -> Callable  # returns a wrapper factory
- fallback_contract: List[Callable[[StreamContext], Optional[NonStreamResult]]]  # chain executed on primary handler failure

Example usage (informal):
from redwood.streams import compose_decorators, telemetry_decorator, decode_decorator

@compose_decorators([telemetry_decorator, decode_decorator])
def user_handler(event):
    # user consumes events as they arrive; decorators add decoding + telemetry
    pass

# SDK will call: wrapped_handler = compose_decorators([...])(user_handler)
# On exception in wrapped_handler, SDK will iterate fallback_contract until a non-None result is returned.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes compose_decorators that preserves event order and cancel semantics
Fallback contract executed on handler failure; at least one built-in fallback provided: non-streaming completion and cached-prefix
Diagnostic token (trace id + stream seq) included on all emitted events and surfaced in Console telemetry
Unit + integration test coverage for: decorator chaining, cancel path, fallback invocation, and race under abrupt transport close
Migration shim provided so existing handler-based consumers continue working with no code change
updates: 2026-02-10: Ticket created. Initial spike completed; prototype compose_decorators implemented in prototype/compose_patch branch. Found ordering ambiguity when mixing transport-level decorators with decode-level decorators.

2026-02-13: Design decision: use FIFO decorator ordering (wraps applied left-to-right) so developer expectation matches call-site order. Rationale: predictable for middleware that pre-processes prefixes (e.g., decoding) before telemetry or transport wrappers.

2026-02-16: Implemented fallback_chain abstraction and two built-in fallbacks: (1) fallback_non_streaming_completion, (2) fallback_cached_prefix. Added circuit_hint object to allow upstream routing to prefer cheaper/safer fallbacks.

2026-02-19: Prototype PR opened. Early QA shows race condition when handler raises while cancel token is racing with transport close; root cause: non-atomic checkpoint update in stream adapter. Added atomic checkpoint guard and reworked cancel propagation to use CancelScope pattern.

2026-02-23: UX review w/ Developer Experience (Maya): updated examples to show decorator composition via function decorator syntax and a builder pattern. Decided to surface a thin shim to keep old handler shape compatible.

2026-02-26: PR updated; added integration test that simulates abrupt network close at 50-75% token emission. Tests currently flaky in CI due to thread scheduling; investigating with deterministic scheduler in test harness.
2026-02-27: Added diagnostic_token stamping for each event and Console telemetry mapping. Updated PR with test flakiness fix (explicit event loop drain) and requested reviewers.
notes:
Trade-offs considered:
- Option A: implicit decorator ordering (auto-detect transport vs decode) — chosen against because brittle.
- Option B: explicit FIFO ordering with helper aliases — chosen for predictability.

Telemetry plan: emit event meta: {diagnostic_token, handler_id, seq, latency_ms, fallback_used} and map to Console trace explorer.

Migration: add 'compat_handler_adapter' that wraps older handlers into new decorator shape; this will be the default until next major release.

Open questions:
- Do we need to expose a preflight hook to run cheap fallback checks before invoking the streaming handler? (benefit: avoid expensive warm-up if fallback will be used)
- Should the fallback chain be async-first (await each fallback) or sync-first? Current prototype supports async callables; prefer async to allow network calls (cache lookups) during fallback.

QA checklist:
- deterministic scheduler tests for cancel/race
- fuzz harness with random decorator orders and induced exceptions
- perf benchmark to measure decorator overhead (<5% token throughput impact target)

testing_summary:
Unit tests: compose order, cancel propagation, single-fallback success, fallback chain exhaustion.
Integration: simulated transport failure, cached-prefix fallback end-to-end.
Known flaky test: stream_race_close_integration fixed by loop-drain approach; rerunning CI.
next_steps: Address remaining race conditions reported by CI and complete flaky test stabilization
Collect perf numbers with and without two decorators (decode + telemetry) and optimize common paths
Post-review: add docs page to SDK reference and a migration note for existing handlers
Schedule follow-up ticket to port pattern to TypeScript and Go SDKs based on this API
